14:1: We have already discussed the separate letters at the beginning of the surahs. A Book We have revealed to you meaning this is a Book We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, and it is the Great Qur’an, which is the most honorable Book that God has revealed from the heavens, to the most honorable Messenger that God has sent to the earth to all its people, Arabs and non-Arabs. That you may bring mankind out of darkness into the light meaning that We have only sent you, O Muhammad, with this Book to bring mankind out of the misguidance and error they are in, to guidance and righteousness, as God the Almighty said: “God is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darkness into the light. But as for those who disbelieve, their allies are false gods. They bring them out from the light into darkness” (al-An’am 2:17). And God the Almighty said: It is He who sends down to His Servant clear verses that He may bring you out from darkness into the light (al-An’am 2:17). And His statement: By the permission of their Lord means He is the guide for whomever He has destined to be guided by the hand of His Messenger sent by His command, guiding them to the path of the Mighty, meaning the Mighty who is not prevented or overcome, rather He is the Subduer of all that is besides Him, the Praiseworthy, meaning the Praised One in all His actions, words, laws, commands, and prohibitions, the Truthful in His report. And His statement: God to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, some of them read it as a new, raised nominative case, and others read it as an attribute of majesty, like the statement of the Most High: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth’ (al-Baqarah 2:17). And His statement: And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment meaning woe to them on the Day of Resurrection, since they opposed you, O Muhammad, and denied you. Then He described them as preferring the life of this world over the Hereafter, meaning they give it precedence and prefer it over it and work for this world, and they forgot the Hereafter and left it behind them. And they hinder [people] from the path of God which is following the messengers. And they desire to make it crooked meaning they desire for the path of God to be crooked, inclined, and crooked, while it is straight in itself and is not harmed by those who oppose it or those who let it down. So in their seeking that, they are in ignorance and misguidance, far from the truth. There is no hope for them in this state of improvement.

14:4: This is from His kindness to His creation that He sends to them messengers from among themselves in their languages, so that they may understand from them what they want and what they were sent with, as Imam Ahmad narrated: Waki’ told us on the authority of Umar ibn Dharr, who said: Mujahid said on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty did not send a prophet except in the language of his people. And His saying: God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills meaning after the clarification and the establishment of the proof against them, God misguides whom He wills from the path of guidance, and guides whom He wills to the truth. And He is the Exalted in Might whatever He wills will be, and whatever He does not will will not be, the Wise in His actions, so He misguides whomever deserves to be misguided and guides whomever is worthy of that. And this was His way with His creation, that He did not send a prophet to a nation unless he was in their language, so He singled out every prophet to convey his message to his nation and not to others, and Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was singled out for the generality of the message to all people, as was proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given five things that were not given to any of the prophets before me: I was aided by terror for a distance of a month’s journey, and the earth was made for me a place of prostration and purification, and spoils of war were made lawful for me while they were not made lawful for anyone before me, and I was given intercession, and a prophet was sent to his people specifically and I was sent to all people.” And there are evidences for this from many aspects. God Almighty said: Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all.’
14:5: God Almighty says: And just as We sent you, O Muhammad, and revealed to you the Book so that you may bring forth all people, calling them to come out from darkness into the light, so We sent Moses to the Children of Israel with Our signs. Mujahid said: They are the nine signs, Bring forth your people, meaning We commanded him, saying to him, Bring forth your people from darkness into the light, meaning call them to goodness so that they may come forth from the darkness of what they were in of ignorance and misguidance into the light of guidance and insight of faith, and remind them of the days of God, meaning His favors and blessings upon them in bringing them out from the captivity of Pharaoh and his subjugation, oppression and tyranny, and His saving them from their enemy, and His splitting the sea for them, and His shading them with clouds, and His sending down upon them manna and quails, and other blessings. Mujahid, Qatadah and more than one other said this. The hadith attributed to the Prophet, which was narrated by Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal in his father’s Musnad, where he said, Yahya bin Abdullah, the client of the Children of Israel, told me. Hashim, Muhammad bin Abaan Al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the words of God Almighty: And remind them of the days of God, he said: of the blessings of God. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad bin Abaan, and Abdullah, his son, also narrated it as a narration that ends with him, and it is more likely. And His statement: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful. That is, in what We did to Our allies, the Children of Israel, when We saved them from the hand of Pharaoh and delivered them from the humiliating torment they were in, there is a lesson for everyone patient, that is, grateful in adversity, that is, in prosperity, as Qatada said: The best servant is a servant who, when afflicted, is patient, and when given, is grateful. And likewise it came in the Sahih on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The whole affair of the believer is amazing. God does not decree for him a decree except that it is good for him. If adversity befalls him, he is patient, and so it is good for him. And if prosperity befalls him, he is grateful, and so it is good for him.”
14:6: The Almighty says, informing about Moses when he mentioned to his people the days of God with them and His blessings upon them, when He saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and what they were subjecting them to of torment and humiliation, as they were slaughtering whoever they found of their sons, and leaving their females, so God saved them from that, and this is a great blessing, and for this reason He said: And in that is a great trial from your Lord meaning a great blessing from Him upon you in that, you are unable to give thanks for it. And it was said: And in what the people of Pharaoh were doing to you of those actions a trial meaning a great test, and it is possible that what is meant is this and that, and God knows best, like the Almighty's saying: And We tested them with good and bad that perhaps they would return. His saying: And when your Lord announced means He announced to you and informed you of His promise to you. It is possible that the meaning is: And when your Lord swore and swore by His glory, majesty and pride, like the Almighty’s saying: And when your Lord announced that He would send against them until the Day of Resurrection. And His saying: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you meaning if you are grateful for My blessings upon you, I will surely increase them for you, but if you are ungrateful meaning if you are ungrateful for the blessings and conceal them and deny them, indeed, My punishment is severe, by taking them away from them and punishing them for their ingratitude. It was mentioned in the hadith: Indeed, a servant is deprived of provision because of the sin he commits. In Al-Musnad, it is narrated that a beggar passed by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he gave him a date, but he was displeased with it and did not accept it. Then another passed by and he gave it to him, but he accepted it and said: A date from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So he ordered forty dirhams for him, or something like that. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad told us, Ammarah al-Saydalani told us on the authority of Thabit on the authority of Anas, who said: A beggar came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he ordered for him a date, but he did not take it or he was afraid of it. He said: Another came to him and he ordered for him a date, and he said: Glory be to God, a date from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So he said to the girl: Go to Umm Salamah and give him the forty dirhams that she has. This was narrated only by Imam Ahmad, and Ammarah ibn Zadhan was deemed trustworthy by Ibn Hibban, Ahmad, and Yaqub ibn Sufyan. Ibn Ma’in said: He is trustworthy. Abu Zur’ah said: There is nothing wrong with him. Abu Hatim said: His hadith should be written down but it should not be used as evidence, because it is not strong. Al-Bukhari said: He may be confused in his hadith. Ahmad also said: He narrated strange hadiths. Abu Dawud said: He is not like that. Al-Daraqutni declared him weak. Ibn Adi said: He is fine for someone whose hadith is written. And the Almighty said: “And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy.” That is, He is Free of need of the gratitude of His servants, and He is the Praiseworthy, the Praised, even if those who disbelieve disbelieve in Him, as He said: If you disbelieve, then indeed, God is Free of need of you. And His saying: But they disbelieved and turned away, and God was Free of need and Praiseworthy. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he narrates on the authority of his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, that he said: “O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, and the humans of you and the jinn of you, to be as pious as the most wicked heart of any one man among you, that would not increase My kingdom in the least. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, and the humans of you and the jinn of you to be as wicked as the most wicked heart of any man among you, that would not decrease My kingdom in the least. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, and the humans of you and the jinn of you to stand on a single plain and ask of Me, and I were to give each person what he asked for, that would not decrease My kingdom in the least, any more than a needle decreases the sea if put into it.” So glory be to Him, the Most High, the Rich, the Praiseworthy.

14:9: Ibn Jarir said: This is part of what Moses said to his people, meaning his reminding them of the days of God's vengeance on the nations that denied the messengers. What Ibn Jarir said is questionable, and it appears that it is a new report from God the Almighty to this nation, as it has been said that the story of 'Aad and Thamud is not in the Torah. If this was from the speech of Moses to his people and his story to them, there is no doubt that these two stories would be in the Torah, and God knows best. In short, God the Almighty has told us the story of the people of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, and other nations that denied the messengers, whose number is only known to God the Almighty. "Their messengers came to them with clear proofs," meaning with clear, dazzling, decisive arguments and evidence. Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said regarding His statement: "None knows them except God," the genealogists lied. And 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: We did not find anyone who knows what came after Ma'ad ibn Adnan. His saying: And they put their hands over their mouths The commentators differed in its meaning. It was said: Its meaning is that they pointed to the mouths of the messengers by ordering them to be silent about them when they called them to God the Almighty. It was said: Rather, they put their hands over their mouths in denial of them. It was said: Rather, it is an expression of their silence about answering the messengers. Mujahid, Muhammad bin Ka’b and Qatadah said: Its meaning is that they denied them and responded to their words with their mouths. Ibn Jarir said: Its explanation is that fi here means ba. He said: It was heard from the Arabs: May God admit you into Paradise, meaning in Paradise. The poet said: I would rather have it than Laqit and his gang, but I would not have it than Sinbas. He wants to desire it. I said: Mujahid supports the interpretation of that with the entire statement: And they said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed, we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us.’ So it is as if this - and God knows best - is an interpretation of the meaning of: So they put their hands to their mouths. Sufyan al-Thawri and Isra’il said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas on the authority of Abdullah regarding his statement: So they put their hands to their mouths, he said: They bit them in rage. Shu’bah said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Hubayrah ibn Yarim, on the authority of Abdullah that he also said that. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam chose it, and Ibn Jarir directed it as his choice with the statement of God the Almighty about al-Munafiqun 63:And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When they heard the speech of God, they were amazed and put their hands to their mouths and said: We have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent, the verse, saying: We do not believe you in what you have brought, for we have strong doubts about it.
14:10: The Almighty tells us about the argument that took place between the disbelievers and their messengers, and that is that when their nations confronted them with doubt about what they brought them of worshipping God alone with no partner, the messengers said: Is there any doubt about God? This could mean two things one of them is there any doubt about His existence, for the nature bears witness to His existence and is created to acknowledge Him, for acknowledging Him is necessary in sound natures, but some of them may be exposed to doubt and confusion, so they need to look into the evidence that leads to His existence, and for this reason the messengers said to them, guiding them to the path of knowing Him as the Originator of the heavens and the earth who created them and innovated them without a previous example, for the evidence of occurrence, creation and subjugation is apparent on them, so they must have a Maker, and He is God, there is no god but God, He is the Creator of everything and its God and King, and the second meaning in their saying: Is there any doubt about God? i.e. is there any doubt about His divinity and His uniqueness in requiring worship of Him, and He is the Creator of all existences, and no one deserves worship except Him alone, with no partner for Him, for Most nations acknowledged the Creator, but worshipped other intermediaries along with Him that they thought would benefit them or bring them closer to God. Their messengers said to them: He calls you to forgive you your sins meaning in the Hereafter and to delay you for a specified term meaning in this world, as God Almighty said: And if you ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him, He will grant you good enjoyment for a specified term and will give to every possessor of virtue his virtue verse. So the nations said to them, arguing about the position of the message after estimating their submission to the first position, and the gist of what they said is: You are only human beings like us meaning how can we follow you based on your mere words when we do not see a miracle from you, Then bring us a clear authority meaning a supernatural one that we propose to you. “Their messengers said to them: We are only human beings like you” meaning it is true that we are human beings like you in humanity, but God bestows favor upon whom He wills of His servants meaning with the message and prophethood, and it was not for us to bring you an authority according to what you asked for except by God’s permission meaning after we asked Him. And His permission for us in that, And in God let the believers put their trust, meaning in all their affairs. Then the messengers said, And why should we not put our trust in God? meaning, what prevents us from putting our trust in Him, when He has guided us to the straightest, clearest, and most evident paths? And we will surely be patient over what you have harmed us with, meaning, from the bad words and foolish actions. And in God let the trustful put their trust.

14:18: This is an example that God the Almighty gave for the deeds of the disbelievers who worshipped other than Him, denied His Messengers, and built their deeds on an incorrect foundation, so they collapsed and were annihilated when they were most in need of them. God the Almighty said: The example of those who disbelieved in their Lord is their deeds meaning the example of their deeds on the Day of Resurrection when they sought reward for them from God the Almighty, because they thought that they were on something but found nothing, and they did not find anything except what is obtained from ashes when a violent wind blows on them on a stormy day meaning one with a strong, violent wind. They were not able to do anything of the deeds they earned in this world except as they are able to collect these ashes on this day, like the Almighty’s saying: And We will present to them whatever deeds they did and make them as scattered dust and His saying: “The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind in which there is a chill that strikes the crops of a people who wronged themselves and destroyed them. It was not God who wronged them, but they wronged themselves” and His saying: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury, as does one who spends his wealth [only] to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the Last Day. His example is like that of a smooth rock upon which is dust, then a downpour strikes it and leaves it bare. They are not able to do anything about what they have earned. And God does not guide the disbelieving people. And His statement in this verse, That is what is far astray, means their efforts and actions are without foundation or rectitude, until they lost their reward when they were most in need of it. That is what is far astray.
14:19: The Almighty says, informing about His ability to resurrect bodies on the Day of Resurrection, that He created the heavens and the earth, which are greater than the creation of people. Is He not the One who was able to create these heavens in their height, vastness, and greatness, and what is in them of fixed and moving planets, and various movements, and dazzling signs, and this earth with what is in it of cradles, valleys, and pegs, and wildernesses and deserts, and wastelands and seas, and trees and plants, and animals of different kinds, benefits, shapes, and colors? Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary of their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, He is over all things competent. And the Almighty said: “Has not man seen that We created him from a sperm-drop? Then at once he is a clear adversary. And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, ‘Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?’ Say, ‘He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation.’ Who made for you fire from the green tree, and then at once you kindle from it. Is not He who The Creator of the heavens and the earth is able to create the likes of them. Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. * His command when He intends a thing is only to say to it, Be, and it is. * So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned. And His statement, If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation. * And that is not difficult for God." That is, it is great and not impossible. Rather, it is easy for Him if you disobey His command to do away with you and bring others who are not like you, as He said, "O mankind, you are those in need of God, while God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. * If He wills, He can do away with you and bring a new creation. * And that is not difficult for God. And He said, And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you. And He said, O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - God will bring forth a people He will love and who will love Him. And He said, If He wills, He can do away with you, O mankind, and bring forth others. And ever is God competent to do that."

14:21: God Almighty says: And they came forth meaning all creatures, good and bad, came forth before God, the One, the Subduer, meaning they gathered for Him in a clearing on the earth, which is a place where there is nothing to cover anyone. Then the weak ones said, meaning the followers of their leaders, masters and notables to those who were arrogant about worshipping God alone, without partner, and about agreeing with the messengers. They said to them: Indeed, we were your followers meaning whatever you ordered us, we obeyed and did. So can you protect us from the punishment of God at all? meaning can you ward off from us any of the punishment of God as you used to promise us and hope for? The leaders said to them: If God had guided us, we would have guided you, but the word of our Lord came true upon us, and God's decree preceded concerning us and you, and the word of punishment came true upon the disbelievers. "It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient. There is no escape for us" meaning there is no escape for us from what we are in if we are patient with it or impatient with it. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: The people of Hell said to each other: Come, for the people of Paradise have only reached Paradise through their weeping and supplication to God, the Almighty. Come, let us weep and supplicate to God. So they wept and supplicated. When they saw that it would not benefit them, they said: The people of Paradise have only reached Paradise through patience. Come, so that we may be patient. So they were patient with a patience the like of which had never been seen, but that did not benefit them. At that point, they said: It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient. I said: It appears that this review will be in Hell after they have entered it, as God, the Almighty, said: “And when they dispute in the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, ‘Indeed, we were your followers, so can you relieve us of a share of the Fire?’ Those who were arrogant will say, ‘Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, God has judged between His servants.’” And God, the Almighty, said: “He will say, ‘Enter among nations that have passed on before you of jinn and mankind into the Fire. 14:24: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, An example of a good word is the testimony that there is no god but God is like a good tree which is the believer, its root is firm he says: there is no god but God in the heart of the believer, and its branches are in the heaven he says that the believer’s deeds are raised to the heavens, and thus Ad-Dahhak, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ikrimah, Mujahid and more than one said: that this is an expression of the believer’s deeds, his good words, and his righteous deeds, and the believer is like a palm tree whose righteous deeds are raised for him at all times and hours, morning and evening, and thus As-Suddi narrated it on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud who said: it is the palm tree, and Shu’bah on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah on the authority of Anas: it is the palm tree. He said: It is the palm tree. And it was narrated from this source and from others on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission ending with him. And this is what Masruq, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Sa`id bin Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others stated. Al-Bukhari said: Ubayd ibn Ismail narrated to us on the authority of Abu Usamah, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “Tell me about a tree that resembles a Muslim man. Its leaves do not fall in summer or winter, and it produces its fruit at all times by the permission of its Lord.” Ibn Umar said: It occurred to me that it was the palm tree, and I saw Abu Bakr and Umar not speaking, so I hated to speak. When they did not say anything, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree. When we got up, I said to Umar: O my father, by God, it occurred to me that it was the palm tree. He said: What prevented you from speaking? I said: I did not see you speaking, so I hated to speak or say anything. Umar said: For you to have said it would be dearer to me than such and such. Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: I accompanied Ibn Umar to Madinah and I did not hear him narrate from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except one hadith. He said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a date-palm was brought to him, so he said: Among the trees is a tree the size of a Muslim man. I wanted to say that it was the palm tree, but I looked and saw that I was the youngest of the people, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree. They both narrated it. Malik and Abdul Aziz narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day to his companions: Among the trees is a tree whose leaves do not fall like the leaves of a believer. He said: It occurred to me among the trees of the valley, and it occurred to me that it was the palm tree, but I was embarrassed until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree. They also narrated it. Shall I not tell you of a deed whose root is in the earth and whose branch is in the sky? He said: What is it, O Messenger of God? That is its root in the earth and its branch is in the sky.” And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, like a good tree, he said: It is a tree in Paradise. And His statement: It brings forth its fruit at all times, it was said: Morning and evening, and it was said: Every month, and it was said: Every two months, and it was said: Every six months, and it was said: Every seven months. It was said: every year. What is apparent from the context is that the believer is like a tree from which fruit continues to be found at all times, summer or winter, night or day. Likewise, the believer continues to have righteous deeds raised up for him during the night and the ends of the day at all times and moments by the permission of its Lord, meaning complete, good, abundant, pleasant, and blessed. And God presents examples for the people that perhaps they will remember. And the Almighty’s saying: And the likeness of a bad word is like a bad tree. This is a likeness of the disbelief of the disbeliever that has no basis or stability. It is likened to the colocynth tree, which is called the artery. Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah on the authority of Anas ibn Malik: It is the colocynth tree. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar al-Hafiz said: Yahya ibn Muhammad al-Sakn narrated to us, Abu Zaid Sa’id ibn al-Rabi’ narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah on the authority of Anas, I think he traced it back to the Prophet, who said: The likeness of a good word is like a good tree. He said: It is the palm tree. And the likeness of a bad word is like a bad tree. He said: It is the artery. Then he narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna on the authority of Ghundar on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Mu’awiyah on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission ending with him. He said: Ghassan told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Shu`ayb, on the authority of Anas, that a veil was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “The parable of a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches are in the sky.
