When we got up, I said to Umar: O my father, by God, it occurred to me that it was the palm tree. He said: What prevented you from speaking? I said: I did not see you speaking, so I hated to speak or say anything. Umar said: For you to have said it would be dearer to me than such and such. Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: I accompanied Ibn Umar to Madinah and I did not hear him narrate from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except one hadith. He said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a date-palm was brought to him, so he said: Among the trees is a tree the size of a Muslim man. I wanted to say that it was the palm tree, but I looked and saw that I was the youngest of the people, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree. They both narrated it. Malik and Abdul Aziz narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day to his companions: Among the trees is a tree whose leaves do not fall like the leaves of a believer. He said: It occurred to me among the trees of the valley, and it occurred to me that it was the palm tree, but I was embarrassed until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is the palm tree. They also narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Abaan - meaning Ibn Zaid Al-Attar - told us, Qatada told us that a man said: O Messenger of God, the wealthy have taken all the rewards. He said: Tell me, if someone were to aim for worldly goods and ride one on top of the other, would it reach the sky? Shall I not tell you of a deed whose root is in the earth and whose branch is in the sky? He said: What is it, O Messenger of God? He said: “Say: There is no god but God, God is the Greatest, Glory be to God, and Praise be to God, ten times after every prayer. That is its root in the earth and its branch is in the sky.” And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, like a good tree, he said: It is a tree in Paradise. And His statement: It brings forth its fruit at all times, it was said: Morning and evening, and it was said: Every month, and it was said: Every two months, and it was said: Every six months, and it was said: Every seven months. It was said: every year. What is apparent from the context is that the believer is like a tree from which fruit continues to be found at all times, summer or winter, night or day. Likewise, the believer continues to have righteous deeds raised up for him during the night and the ends of the day at all times and moments by the permission of its Lord, meaning complete, good, abundant, pleasant, and blessed. And God presents examples for the people that perhaps they will remember. And the Almighty’s saying: And the likeness of a bad word is like a bad tree. This is a likeness of the disbelief of the disbeliever that has no basis or stability. It is likened to the colocynth tree, which is called the artery. Shu’bah narrated it on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah on the authority of Anas ibn Malik: It is the colocynth tree. Abu Bakr al-Bazzar al-Hafiz said: Yahya ibn Muhammad al-Sakn narrated to us, Abu Zaid Sa’id ibn al-Rabi’ narrated to us, Shu’bah narrated to us on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah on the authority of Anas, I think he traced it back to the Prophet, who said: The likeness of a good word is like a good tree. He said: It is the palm tree. And the likeness of a bad word is like a bad tree. He said: It is the artery. Then he narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna on the authority of Ghundar on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Mu’awiyah on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission ending with him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Musa bin Ismail told us, Hammad - he is Ibn Salamah - told us, on the authority of Shu`ayb bin Al-Habhab, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The example of a bad word is like a bad tree, which is the colocynth. So I told Abu Al-`Aliyah about that, and he said: This is how we used to hear it. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah. Abu Ya`la narrated it in his Musnad in a more detailed manner than this. He said: Ghassan told us, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Shu`ayb, on the authority of Anas, that a veil was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “The parable of a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firmly fixed and its branches are in the sky. It brings forth its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord.” He said: It is the palm tree. “And the parable of a bad word is like a bad tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability.” He said: It is the colocynth. Shu`ayb said: So I informed Abu al-`Aliyah of that, and he said: That is how we used to hear it. His statement: uprooted means uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability means it has no root and no stability. Likewise, disbelief has no root and no branches, and no deed of the disbeliever ascends, and nothing is accepted from him.
14:27: Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid told us, Shu`bah told us, Alqamah ibn Murthad told me: I heard Sa`d ibn `Ubaydah on the authority of al-Bara` ibn `Azib, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a Muslim is asked in the grave, he will testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. This is what He said: ‘God will confirm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter.’” Muslim also narrated it, as did the rest of the group, all from the hadith of Shu`bah. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the funeral of a man from the Ansar. We reached the grave and it had not yet been dug. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat down, and we sat around him as if there were birds on our heads. He had a stick in his hand with which he was poking the ground. He raised his head and said: Seek refuge with God from the punishment of the grave two or three times. Then he said: “When the believing servant is at a severance from this world and is entering the Hereafter, angels descend to him from the heavens with white faces, as if their faces were the sun, with them a shroud from the shrouds of Paradise and embalming from the embalming of Paradise until they sit near him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes and sits at his head and says: O good soul, come out to forgiveness from God and His pleasure.” He said: “So it comes out flowing, as a drop flows from the mouth of a waterskin. He takes it, and when he takes it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye until they take it and put it in that.” The shroud and in that is the embalming, and from it comes out the best scent of musk found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it and they do not pass by it - meaning by a group of angels - except that they say: What is this good soul? They say: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, by the best of the names they used to call him by in the world, until they reach the lowest heaven and they ask permission for him, and it is opened for him and those closest to him accompany him from every heaven to the heaven that follows it, until he reaches the seventh heaven, and God says: Write the book of My servant in the highest and return him to the earth, for from it I created them and in it I will return them, and from it I will bring them out another time. His soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and make him sit up and say to him: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. They say to him: What is your religion? He says: My religion is Islam. They say to him: Who is this man who was sent among you? He says: He is the Messenger of God. They say to him: What is your knowledge? He says: I read the Book of God and believed in it and confirmed it. Then a voice calls from the heaven: My servant has told the truth, so furnish him from Paradise, clothe him from Paradise, and open for him a door to Paradise. He said: Then some of its spirit and its fragrance comes to him, and his grave is expanded for him as far as his sight can reach. Then a man with a handsome face, handsome clothes, and a pleasant scent comes to him and says: Be glad with that which pleases you. This is your day which you were promised. Then he says to him: Who are you? Your face is the face that brings goodness? He says: I am your good deed. He says: O Lord, establish the Hour, O Lord, establish the Hour, so that I may return to my family and my wealth. He said: And when the disbelieving servant is in a state of separation from this world and coming to the Hereafter, angels with black faces descend to him from the heavens, carrying sackcloth, and they sit from him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes and sits at his head and says: O wicked soul, come out to the wrath and anger of God. He said: So it spreads through his body and pulls it out as a skewer is pulled out of wet wool. He takes it, and when he takes it, he does not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye until they put it in that sackcloth, and it comes out of it like the foulest odor of a corpse found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it and they do not pass by it by a group of angels except that they say: What is this wicked soul? They say: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, with the worst names he was called by in this world, until he reaches the lowest heaven, and he asks permission for it but it is not granted to him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. God says: Write his book in Sijjin in the lowest earth. Then his soul is thrown out. Then he recited: And whoever associates others with God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and was snatched by birds or the wind swept him to a remote place. Then his soul is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and make him sit up and say to him: Who is your Lord? He says: Huh, huh, I do not know. They say to him: What is your religion? He says: Huh, huh, I do not know. They say to him: Who is this man who was sent among you? He will say: Huh, huh, I do not know. Then a voice will call from the heaven: My servant has lied, so spread out for him a bed from the Fire and open for him a door to the Fire. Then some of its heat and poisonous winds will come to him, and his grave will be constricted until his ribs overlap. Then a man with an ugly face, ugly clothes, and a foul odor will come to him and say: Receive good report of that which will displease you. This is the day which you were promised. He will say: Who are you, for your face is the face that brings evil? He will say: I am your evil deeds. He will say: O Lord, do not establish the Hour. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Al-A’mash, and Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Al-Munhal bin Amr with it. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Habib, on the authority of al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn Azib, may God be pleased with him, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to a funeral, and he mentioned something similar, and in it: “So when his soul departs, every angel between heaven and earth and every angel in heaven prays for him, and the gates of heaven are opened, and there is no one at a gate except that they call upon God Almighty to ascend with his soul before them.” And at the end of it: “Then a blind, deaf, and mute man will be appointed for him, and in his hand will be a hammer, if he struck a mountain with it it would be dust, so he strikes him a blow and he becomes dust, then God Almighty returns him to how he was, so he strikes him another blow and he cries out a cry that everything hears except the two heavy things.” Al-Bara’ said: Then a door to Hell will be opened for him and carpets of Hell will be prepared for him. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khaithamah, on the authority of al-Bara’ regarding God Almighty’s statement: God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, he said: the torment of the grave. Al-Masoudi said on the authority of Abdullah bin Mukhariq on the authority of his father on the authority of Abdullah who said: When a believer dies, he is seated in his grave and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet? God will make him steadfast and he will say: My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah recited: God will make firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. Imam Abd bin Hamid, may God have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: Yunus bin Muhammad told us, Shaiban bin Abd al-Rahman told us on the authority of Qatada, Anas bin Malik told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a servant is placed in his grave, and his companions turn away from him, and he hears the sound of their sandals, two angels come to him and make him sit and say to him: What did you say about this man? He said: As for the believer, he will say: I bear witness that he is the servant and Messenger of God. He said: It will be said to him: Look at your seat in Hell, God has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise.” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So he will see them both. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that his grave will be expanded to seventy cubits and filled with greenery until the Day of Resurrection. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abd bin Hamid, and narrated by al-Nasa’i from Hadith of Yunus bin Muhammad Al-Mu’addab. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he asked Jabir bin Abdullah about the two trials of the grave, and he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “This nation will be tested in its graves. When the believer is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, a severe, scolding angel will come to him and say to him: What did you say about this man? As for the believer, he will say: He is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and His servant. The angel will say to him: Look at your seat that you had in Hell, God has saved you from it and replaced your seat that you see in Hell with the seat that you see in Paradise. He will see both of them, and the believer will say: Let me give good report to my family. He will be told: Be still. As for the hypocrite, he will sit when his family turns away from him and it will be said to him: What did you say about this man? He will say: I do not know, I say as the people say. He will be told: I did not know. This is your seat that you had in Paradise, and its place has been replaced by your seat in Hell.” Jabir said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Everyone will be resurrected. A slave in the grave remains as he died, the believer remains as he was, and the hypocrite remains as he was. Its chain of transmission is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, but it was not included by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Aamer told us, Abbad bin Rashid told us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: We witnessed a funeral with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, this nation will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his companions disperse, an angel will come to him with an iron hammer in his hand and make him sit. He will say: What do you say about this man? If he is a believer, he will say: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. He will say to him: You have spoken the truth. Then a door to Hell will be opened for him. He will say: This would have been your home had you disbelieved in your Lord. But now that you have believed, this is your home. Then a door to Paradise will be opened for him. He will want to go up to it, but it will be said to him: Dwell, and his grave will be made spacious for him. If he is a disbeliever or a hypocrite, he will say: What do you say about this man? He will say: I do not know. I heard people say something. He will say: You neither knew nor followed, nor were you guided. Then a door will be opened for him.” A door to Paradise, and he says to him: This is your home if you believe in your Lord, but if you disbelieve in Him, then God the Almighty will replace it for you. So he opens for him a door to Hell, then he crushes him with a hammer, and he cries out a cry that all of God’s creation hears, except for the two heavy ones. Some of the people said: O Messenger of God, no one has an angel standing over him holding a hammer except that he is crushed at that time. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God makes firm those who believe with the firm word. This is also a chain of transmission that is not bad, because Ibad bin Rashid al-Tamimi was narrated by al-Bukhari in conjunction, but some of them weakened it. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us from Ibn Abi Tha’lab, from Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, from Sa’id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The angels attend the dead. If it is a righteous man, they say: ‘Come out, O good soul, you were in a good body. Come out praiseworthy and receive good tidings of a spirit and fragrant water and a Lord who is not angry.’ He said: ‘It will continue to be said to it until it comes out. Then it will be taken up to heaven and it will be opened for it. It will be asked: Who is this?’ It will be said: So-and-so. They will say: ‘Welcome to the good soul that was in a good body. Enter praiseworthy and receive good tidings of a spirit and fragrant water and a Lord who is not angry.’ He said: ‘It will continue to be said to it until it reaches the heaven in which God Almighty is.’ And if it is a bad man, they will say: ‘Come out, O evil soul, you were in an evil body. Come out blameworthy and receive good tidings of boiling water and pus, and other similar pairs.’ It will continue to be said to it until it comes out. Then it will be taken up to heaven and it will be opened for it and it will be said: Who is this?’ It is said: So-and-so. It is said: No welcome to the evil soul that was in the evil body. Go back, you who are reprehensible, for the gates of heaven will not be opened for you. So he is sent from heaven and then he goes to the grave. The righteous man sits and is told what was said to him in the first hadith. The evil man sits and is told what was said to him in the first hadith. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b in a similar manner. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him, he said: When the soul of a believing slave leaves, two angels meet it and ascend with it. Hammad said: He mentioned the pleasantness of its scent and mentioned musk. He said: And the people of the heavens say: A pleasant soul has come from the earth. May God’s blessings be upon you and upon the body that you inhabited. So he is taken to his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and it is said: Take him to the end of his life. And when the soul of the disbeliever leaves - Hammad said - and he mentioned its stench and mentioned its hatred, the people of the heavens say: A foul soul has come from the earth. So it is said: Take him to the end of his life. Abu Hurairah said: So the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) put a patch that was on his nose back like this. Ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Umar ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani told us, Zaid ibn Akram told us, Muadh ibn Hisham told us, my father told me on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Qassam ibn Zuhair, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When a believer is taken, the angels of mercy come to him with white silk and say: ‘Come out to the spirit of God.’ So it comes out like the most fragrant scent of musk, so that some of them hand it to each other so that they can smell it until they bring it to the gate of heaven, and they say: ‘What is this pleasant scent that has come from the earth?’ And they do not come to a heaven except that they say the same thing until they bring it to the spirits of the believers, and they are more joyful for it than the people of the absent one are for their absent one. They say: ‘What happened to so-and-so?’ They say: ‘Leave him until he rests, for he was in sorrow.’ He says: ‘He died. Did he not come to you?’ They say: ‘He went with him to his mother in the abyss.’ As for the disbeliever, the angels of punishment come to him with a sackcloth and say: ‘Come out to the wrath of God.’ So it comes out like a stench.” The wind of a corpse, and it takes him to the door of the earth. It was also narrated on the authority of Hammam bin Yahya on the authority of Abu al-Juza’ on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. He said, “He will ask: What did so-and-so do? What did so-and-so do? What did so-and-so do?” He said: As for the disbeliever, when his soul is taken and he goes with it to the gate of the earth, the keepers of the earth will say: We have not found a smell more foul than this, and it will reach the lowest earth.” Qatada said: A man told me on the authority of Saeed bin al-Musayyab on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr who said: The souls of the believers will gather in Jabiyah, and the souls of the disbelievers will gather in Barhout, a salt marsh in Hadhramaut, then his grave will be made narrow for him. Al-Hafiz Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya bin Khalaf told us, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the dead person - or he said: one of you - is buried, two black and blue angels come to him, one of them is called Munkar and the other Nakir, and they say: What did you say about this man? He says: What did he say? He is the servant of God and His Messenger. I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger. They say: We knew that you would say this. Then his grave is expanded for him seventy cubits by seventy, and it is illuminated for him. Then it is said to him: Sleep. He says: Go back to my family and inform them. They say: Sleep the sleep of a bridegroom who is not awakened except by the most beloved of his family until God raises him from that resting place. And if he was a hypocrite, he says: I heard the people say: So I said the same as them: I do not know. They say: We knew that you would say this. Then it is said: To the earth: It will close on him, and it will close on him until his ribs interlock, and he will remain tormented therein until God raises him from that resting place of his.” Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and strange hadith. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God will make firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. He said: “That is when he is asked in the grave, ‘Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet? ’ He says: ‘My Lord is God, and my religion is Islam, and my Prophet Muhammad came to us with clear proofs from God, so I believed in him and confirmed it. ’ It is said to him: ‘You have told the truth. Upon this you lived, upon this you died, and upon this you will be resurrected. ’” Ibn Jarir said: Mujahid ibn Musa and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Yazid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Amr informed us on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “By the One in Whose hand is my soul, the dead person hears the flapping of your sandals when you turn away from him. If he was a believer, the prayer would be at his head, the zakat would be on his right, and the fasting would be on his left, and doing good deeds such as charity, maintaining ties of kinship, doing good deeds, and being kind to people would be at his grave.” His feet, and he is approached from the head, and the prayer says: There is no entrance before me. He is approached from his right, and the zakat says: There is no entrance before me. He is approached from his left, and the fasting says: There is no entrance before me. He is approached at his feet and says: Doing good deeds has no entrance before me. He is told: Sit down. He sits, and the sun appears to him as if it is about to set. He is told: Tell us what we ask you. He says: Leave me until I pray. He is told: You will do that, so tell us what we ask you. He says: What do you ask me about? He is told: Did you see this man who was among you? What do you say about him, and what do you testify against him? He says: Is he Muhammad? It will be said to him: Yes. He will say: I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God, and that he came to us with clear proofs from God, so we believed him. It will be said to him: On that you lived and on that you died, and on that you will be resurrected, God willing. Then his grave will be expanded for him by seventy cubits and it will be illuminated for him, and a door to Paradise will be opened for him and it will be said to him: Look at what God has prepared for you in it. So his happiness and joy will increase. Then his breath will be placed in the good breath, and it is a green bird that clings to the trees of Paradise, and the body will be returned to the dust it began in. This is the saying of God: God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. Narrated by Ibn Hibban on the authority of Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman on the authority of Muhammad bin Umar, and he mentioned the answer of the disbeliever and his punishment. Al-Bazzar said: Saeed bin Bahr Al-Qaratisi told us, Al-Walid bin Al-Qasim told us, Yazid bin Kaysan told us on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, I think he traced it back to the Prophet, who said: “The believer is brought down by death and sees what he sees, and he wishes that it would come out, meaning his soul, and God loves to meet him. The believer ascends with his soul to the heavens, and the souls of the believers come to him and ask him about their acquaintances among the people of the earth. So if he says: I left so-and-so on the earth, that pleases them, and if he says: So-and-so has died, they say: He was not brought to us. The believer sits in his grave and is asked: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. And he is asked: Who is your Prophet? He says: Muhammad is my Prophet. It is said: What is your religion? He says: My religion is Islam. Then a door is opened for him in his grave and he says - or it is said - Look at your place, then he sees the grave and it is as if it were a sleep. And if death comes down to the enemy of God and he sees what he saw, then he does not like his soul to come out ever, and God hates to meet him, so when he sits in his grave Or he sits down, and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? He says: I do not know. It is said: You did not know. Then a door to Hell is opened for him, then he is struck a blow that every creature hears except the two heavy beasts. Then it is said to him: Sleep as one who is bitten sleeps. I said to Abu Hurairah: Who is one who is bitten? He said: The one who is bitten by beasts and snakes, then his grave is made narrow for him. Then he said: We do not know of anyone who narrated it except Al-Walid bin Al-Qasim. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Hajin bin Al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Salamah Al-Majshun narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, who said: Asma, meaning the daughter of Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with her, used to narrate on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “When a person enters his grave, if he is a believer, his deeds will surround him with prayer and fasting. He said: Then the angel will come to him from the direction of prayer and will turn him back, and from the direction of fasting and will turn him back. He said: Then he will call him, ‘Sit down.’ So he will sit down and say to him: What do you say about this man, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Who? He said: Muhammad. He said: I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God. He said: How do you know that I met him? He said: I bear witness that he is the Messenger of God. He said: He says that I lived upon this, and died upon this, and will be resurrected upon this. But if he was a sinner or a disbeliever, the angel will come to him with nothing between him and him to prevent him, and he will make him sit down and say to him: What do you say about this man? He said: Which man? He said: Muhammad. He said: He will say: By God, I do not know. I heard the people saying something and I said it. The angel will say to him: That is what you lived upon, and died upon this, and you will be resurrected upon this.” He said: “And a beast will be sent to him in his grave, with a whip, and its fruit will be a burning coal like the horn of a camel, and it will beat him as God wills, deaf and unable to hear his voice, so it will have mercy on him.” Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding this verse: When death approaches a believer, the angels attend him, greet him and give him the good report of Paradise. When he dies, they walk with his funeral procession and pray over him with the people. When he is buried, he is seated in his grave and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? He says: My Lord is God. It is said to him: Who is your Messenger? He says: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is said to him: What is your testimony? He says: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. His grave is expanded for him as far as his sight can reach. As for the disbeliever, the angels descend upon him and spread out their hands - spreading out means striking - strike their faces and their backs at death. When he is placed in his grave, he is made to sit and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? He does not respond to them at all, and God makes him forget to mention that. When it is said: Who is the Messenger who was sent to you? He does not find guidance for him and does not respond to them at all. Thus does God mislead the disbelievers. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Othman bin Hakim Al-Awdi told us, Shureih bin Muslimah told us, Ibrahim bin Yusuf told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amer bin Saad Al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu Qatada Al-Ansari, regarding the words of God Almighty: God keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter 1:13, he said: When a believer dies, he is seated in his grave and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? He says: God. He is asked: Who is your prophet? He says: Muhammad bin Abdullah. He is asked that several times, then a door to Hell is opened for him and it is said to him: Look at your home in Hell if you deviate. Then a door to Paradise is opened for him and it is said to him: Look at your home in Paradise if you are steadfast. When a disbeliever dies, he is seated in his grave and it is said to him: Who is your Lord? Who is your prophet? He says: I do not know, I used to hear people say it. He is told: You did not know. Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he is told: Look at your home, if you are steadfast. Then a door to Hell is opened for him, and he is told: Look at your home, if you have deviated. This is what God Almighty says: God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, God will make firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world, he said: There is no god but God, and in the Hereafter, the question is in the grave. Qatada said, as for the life of this world, He will make them firm with goodness and righteous deeds, and in the Hereafter, in the grave. This was also narrated on the authority of more than one of the predecessors. Abu Abdullah Al-Hakim Al-Tirmidhi said in his book Nawader Al-Usul: My father told us, Abdullah bin Nafi’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Fadik, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Abdullah, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us one day while we were in the mosque of Medina, and said: “Last night I saw something amazing. I saw a man from my nation to whom the Angel of Death came to take his soul, but his righteousness towards his parents came and turned it away from him. I saw a man from my nation upon whom the torment of the grave was spread, but his ablution came and saved him from that. I saw a man from my nation surrounded by devils, but the remembrance of God came to him and freed him from them. I saw a man from my nation surrounded by the angels of torment, but his prayer came to him and saved him from their hands. I saw a man from my nation panting with thirst, and whenever he came to a pool he was prevented from it, but his fasting came to him and gave him water and quenched his thirst. I saw a man from my nation while the prophets were sitting.” Circle by circle, whenever he approached a circle they would expel him. Then his ritual bath from major ritual impurity came to him, so he took him by the hand and made him sit beside me. I saw a man from my nation with darkness in front of him, darkness behind him, darkness to his right, darkness to his left, darkness above him, darkness below him, and he was perplexed in it. Then his Hajj and Umrah came to him and extracted him from the darkness and brought him into the light. I saw a man from my nation speaking to the believers but they did not speak to him. Then the ties of kinship came to him and said: O group of believers, speak to him, so they spoke to him. I saw a man from my nation shielding his face from the blazing fire and its sparks with his hand, so his charity came to him and became a veil over his face and a shade over his head. I saw a man from my nation whom the guards had seized from every place, so his command to do good and his prohibition of evil came to him and rescued him from their hands and brought him into the company of the angels of mercy. I saw a man from my nation Kneeling on his knees, between him and God was a veil, then his good character came to him, so He took him by the hand and brought him to God, the Almighty and Majestic. I saw a man from my nation whose record had fallen to his left, then his fear of God came to him, so he took his record and placed it in his right. I saw a man from my nation whose scale had become light, then his excesses came to him and made his scale heavy. I saw a man from my nation standing on the edge of Hell, then his fear of God came to him and rescued him from that and he passed. I saw a man from my nation falling into the Fire, then his tears that he cried out of fear of God in this world came to him, so He extracted him from the Fire. I saw a man from my nation standing on the Bridge, sometimes crawling and sometimes crawling, then his prayers upon me came to him, so I took him by the hand and made him stand and he passed on the Bridge. I saw a man from my nation who reached the gate of Paradise, then the gates were closed in front of him, then the testimony that there is no god came to him. Except for God, so the doors were opened for him and he entered Paradise.” Al-Qurtubi said after citing this hadith from this source: This is a great hadith in which he mentioned specific actions that save from specific terrors. He cited it like this in his book, At-Tadhkirah. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili narrated a strange and lengthy hadith about this, saying: Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Nakri told us, Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Barsani Abu Uthman told us, Abu Asim al-Habti told us, and he was one of the best people of Basra, and he was one of the companions of Hazm and Salam ibn Abi Mut’i’, Bakr ibn Khunais told us, on the authority of Dhirar ibn Amr, on the authority of Yazid al-Raqashi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of Tamim al-Dari, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God Almighty says to the Angel of Death: Go to my friend and bring him to me, for I have struck him with ease and hardship, and I have found him where I like. Bring him to me so that I may comfort him. So the Angel of Death goes to him with five hundred angels with them shrouds and embalming materials from Paradise, and with them bundles of basil, the root of basil is one, and on its head are twenty colors, each color has a scent other than the scent of its companion, and with them is white silk with the most fragrant musk, and the Angel of Death sits at his head and the angels surround him, and each angel of them places his hand on one of his limbs. And that white silk and fragrant musk will be spread under his chin, and a door to Paradise will be opened for him, and his soul will be comforted at that point by the edge of Paradise, sometimes by its spouses, sometimes by its clothing, and sometimes by its fruits, just as a child comforts his family when he cries. He said: His spouses will be delighted at that point, and the soul will emerge. Al-Barsani said: He wants it to emerge from the rush to what it loves. He said: And the Angel of Death will say: Come out, O good soul, to a thornless lote tree, and a banana tree with branches, and an extended shade, and flowing water. He said: And the Angel of Death is more gentle with him than a mother is with her child. He knows that that soul is beloved to his Lord, so he seeks out his gentleness out of love for Him, pleasing the Lord with him, and his soul will be extracted as a hair is extracted from dough. He said: And God Almighty said: Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, and He said: But if he is of those brought near, then there will be rest and fragrance and a Garden of Delight. He said: A soul from the direction of death, and fragrance that meets him, and a Garden of Delight. Naim meets him, he said: So when the Angel of Death takes his soul, the soul says to the body: May God reward you well on my behalf, for you were quick to obey God, and slow to disobey God, so I was saved and you were saved, he said: And the body says the same to the soul, he said: And the regions of the earth in which he obeyed God weep for him, and every gate of the heaven from which his deeds ascend and his provision descend for forty nights, he said: So when the Angel of Death takes his soul, the five hundred angels stay by his body, and the children of Adam do not turn him over to one side except that the angels turn him over before them, and wash him and shroud him in shrouds before the shrouds of the children of Adam, and embalm him before the embalming of the children of Adam, and two rows of angels rise from the door of his house to his grave to meet him with seeking forgiveness, so Satan cries out at that time with a cry from which the bones of his body crack, he said: And he says to his soldiers: Woe to you, how was this servant saved from you? They say: This was an infallible servant. He said: When the Angel of Death ascends with his soul, Gabriel meets him with seventy thousand angels, each bringing him good report from his Lord, in addition to the good report of his companion. He said: When the Angel of Death reaches the Throne with his soul, the soul falls down in prostration. He said: God the Almighty says to the Angel of Death: Go with the soul of My servant and place him in a thornless lote tree, and a banana tree with layers, and an extended shade, and flowing water. He said: When he is placed in his grave, the prayer comes to him and is on his right, and fasting comes to him and is on his left, and the Qur’an comes to him and is at his head, and his walking to prayer comes to him and is at his feet, and patience comes to him and is on the side of the grave. He said: Then God the Almighty sends a neck from the torment. They said: It comes to him from his right. He said: Then the prayer says behind you: By God, he has been steadfast his entire life, and he has only rested now when he is placed in his grave. He said: Then it comes to him from his left and fasting says the same. He said: Then it comes to him from his head and the Qur’an says: And the male is like that. He said: Then it will come to him from his feet and he will say, his walking to prayer is like that, so the punishment will not come to him from a direction he seeks, does he find a way to it except that he will find the friend of God has taken his paradise. He said: Then the punishment will be suppressed at that time and he will come out. He said: And patience will say to all the deeds, but it did not prevent me from undertaking it myself, except that I looked at what you have, so if you are unable, I will be its companion, but if you suffice for him, I will be a reserve for him at the path and the balance. He said: And God will send two angels whose sights are like flashing lightning, and their voices are like pounding thunder, and their fangs are like hawks, and their breaths are like flames, they will tread on their hair between each one’s shoulders a distance of such and such, and compassion and mercy have been taken from them, and they will be called Munkar and Nakir, in the hand of each one of them is a hammer, if Rabi’ah and Mudar were to unite on it they would not be able to lift it. He said: So they will say to him, Sit down. He said: So he will sit and sit upright. He said: And his shrouds will fall on his waist. He said: Then they will say: He said to him: Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your prophet? They said: O Messenger of God, who can speak at that time when you are describing the two angels as you are describing? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God confirms those who believe with the firm word in this world and in the Hereafter. God leaves astray the wrongdoers, and God does what He wills.” He said: He will say: My Lord is God alone, with no partner, and my religion is Islam, which the angels believed in, and my Prophet Muhammad is the Seal of the Prophets. He said: They will say to him: You have spoken the truth. He said: They will push the grave and expand it forty cubits in front of him, forty cubits to his right, forty cubits to his left, forty cubits to his head, and forty cubits to his feet. He said: They will expand it for him two hundred cubits. Al-Barsani said: I think it is forty cubits surrounding him. He said: Then they will say to him: Look above you, and there is an open door to Paradise. He said: They will say to him: This is your home, my friend, since you obeyed God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, at that time a joy will reach his heart that will never return. Then it will be said to him: Look below you. He said: He will look below him and there is an open door to Hell. He said: They say: By God, you have been saved. This is the last thing you have to do. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then a joy will reach his heart at that time that will never return. He said: Aisha said: Seventy-seven doors to Paradise will be opened for him, and its fragrance and coolness will come to him until God Almighty resurrects him. And with the previous chain of transmission to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “And God Almighty says to the Angel of Death: Go to My enemy and bring him to Me, for I have expanded My provision for him and facilitated My blessings for him, but he refused except to disobey Me, so bring him to Me, so that I may take revenge on him. He said: So the Angel of Death goes to him in the most abhorrent form that anyone has ever seen, with twelve eyes, and with him is a skewer of fire, with many thorns, and with him are five hundred angels with them, with them copper and embers from the embers of Hell, and with them are whips of fire to lash out, and it is a blazing fire. He said: So the Angel of Death strikes him with that skewer with a blow that will cause every thorn root from that skewer to disappear into the root of every hair, vein, and nail. He said: Then he twists him violently. He said: So he extracts his soul from the nails of his feet. He said: So he throws it into his heels. He said: So the enemy of God becomes intoxicated at that time, and the Angel of Death relieves him of it. He said: And the angels strike his face and his anus with those whips. He said: So the Angel of Death pulls him up.” Then the Angel of Death pulls him tightly and pulls his soul from his heels and throws it into his knees. Then the enemy of God becomes intoxicated and the Angel of Death lifts him up from him. He said: Then the Angel of Death whips him tightly and pulls his soul from his knees and throws it into his loins. Then the enemy of God becomes intoxicated and the Angel of Death lifts him up from him. He said: Then the Angels whip his face and his backside with those whips. He said: Likewise to his chest and likewise to his throat. He said: Then the Angels spread that copper and the embers of Hell under his chin. He said: And the Angel of Death says: Come out, O cursed soul, to poisonous water and scalding water and a shade of scorching heat that is neither cool nor generous. He said: Then when the Angel of Death takes his soul, the soul says to the body: May God reward you evil on my behalf, for you were quick with me to disobey God and slow with me to obey God. So you have perished and have perished. He said: And the body says the same to the soul, and the regions of the earth on which he disobeyed God curse him, and the soldiers of Satan set out. He said: Then they will bring him the good report that they have brought a slave from the children of Adam to the Fire. He said: Then when he is placed in his grave, his grave will become narrow for him until his ribs overlap, so that the right side enters the left and the left enters the right. He said: And God will send to him black snakes like the necks of camels, they will seize his hare and the big toes of his feet and bite him until they meet in the middle. He said: And God will send two angels whose sight is like lightning, their voices like thunder, their fangs like hawks, and their breaths like flames, they will tread on their hair between the shoulders of each of them for such and such a distance. Compassion and mercy have been taken from them. They will be called Munkar and Nakir. In the hand of each of them is a hammer, if Rabi’ah and Mudar were to unite on it, they would not be able to lift it. He said: Then they will say to him: Sit down. So he sits upright and his shrouds will fall on his waist. He said: Then they will say to him: Who is your Lord, what is your religion, and who is your Prophet? He will say: I do not know. They will say to him: You did not know, nor did you recite. They will strike him with a blow whose sparks will fly into his grave, then they will return. He said: They will say: Look above you. So he will look, and there will be an open door to Paradise. They will say: Enemy of God, this is your home if you had obeyed God. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a regret will reach his heart at that time that will never be reversed. He said: And they will say to him: Look below you. So he will look below him, and there will be an open door to Hell. They will say to him: Enemy of God, this is your home since you disobeyed God. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, a regret will reach his heart at that time that will never be reversed. He said: And Aisha said: And seventy-seven doors to Hell will be opened for him, and its heat and poisonous winds will come to him until God sends him to it. This is a very strange hadith, and a strange context, and Yazid al-Raqashi, its narrator on the authority of Anas, has strange and reprehensible things, and his narration is weak according to the imams, and God knows best. For this reason, Abu Dawud said: Ibrahim bin Musa al-Razi told us, Hisham - he is Ibn Yusuf - told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Buhair on the authority of Hani, the freed slave of Uthman, on the authority of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished burying a man, he would stand over him and say, Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask for him to be steadfast, for he is being questioned now. Abu Dawud is the only one to narrate it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated, when God the Almighty said: And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming pangs of death, while the angels are stretching out their hands al-Baqarah 2:17, a very long hadith with strange chains of transmission on the authority of al-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and it also contains strange things.
14:28: Al-Bukhari said: His statement, Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? Have you not known, like his statement, Have you not seen how "Have you not seen those who went out destruction is perdition, barr yabir yabir, a people of barr" perished. Ali bin Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata. Ibn Abbas heard, "Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief?" He said: They are the disbelievers of the people of Mecca. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, it is Jabalah bin Al-Ayham and those who followed him from the Arabs and joined the Romans. The well-known and correct statement on the authority of Ibn Abbas is the first statement: Even if the meaning includes all disbelievers, then God the Most High sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mercy to the worlds and a blessing to the people, so whoever accepted it and gave thanks for it entered Paradise, and whoever rejected it and disbelieved in it entered Hell. A similar statement was narrated on the authority of Ali, similar to the first statement of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, on the authority of Abi At-Tayyib that Ibn Al-Kawwa’ asked Ali about those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to reside in the home of ruin. He said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh on the day of Badr. Al-Mundhir bin Shadhan told us, Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, Bassam - he is Al-Sayrafi - told us, on the authority of Abi At-Tayyib that he said: A man came to Ali and said: O Commander of the Faithful, who are those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to reside in the home of ruin? He said: The hypocrites of Quraysh. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Nufayl told us that he read to Muqal on the authority of Ibn Abi Husayn that Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said: Is there no one to ask me about the Qur’an? By God, if I knew today someone who knew it better than me, even if he were from across the seas, I would go to him. Abdullah bin Al-Kawwa’ stood up and said: Who are those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to reside in the home of ruin? He said: The polytheists of Quraysh were given the blessing of God, faith, but they exchanged God’s blessing for disbelief and caused their people to reside in the abode of destruction. Al-Suddi said about his statement: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? The verse, Muslim mentioned in Al-Mustawfi, on the authority of Ali, that he said: They are the two most wicked of the Quraysh 106:Banu Umayyah and Banu Al-Mughira. As for Banu Al-Mughira, they caused their people to live in the abode of destruction on the day of Badr, and as for Banu Umayyah, they caused their people to live in the abode of destruction on the day of Uhud. Abu Jahl was on the day of Badr, and Abu Sufyan was on the day of Uhud. As for the abode of destruction, it is Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad bin Yahya told us, Al-Harith Abu Mansur told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, they said: I heard Ali recite this verse: And they caused their people to dwell in the home of destruction. He said: They are the two most wicked of Quraysh 106:Banu Umayyah and Banu Al-Mughira. As for Banu Al-Mughira, they were destroyed on the day of Badr, and as for Banu Umayyah, they were granted respite for a time. Abu Ishaq narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Murrah on the authority of Ali, something similar, and it was narrated from him through other chains of transmission. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd on the authority of Yusuf ibn Sa`d, on the authority of `Umar ibn al-Khattab, regarding his statement: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? He said: They are the two most wicked of the Quraysh 106:Banu al-Mughira and Banu Umayya. As for Banu al-Mughira, you spared them on the day of Badr, and as for Banu Umayya, you were granted respite for a time. Hamza al-Zayyat narrated it in this way on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah, who said: Ibn `Abbas said to `Umar ibn al-Khattab: O Commander of the Faithful, what is this verse: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief and caused their people to dwell in the home of ruin? He said: They are the two most wicked of the Quraysh 106:my maternal uncles and your paternal uncles. As for my maternal uncles, God uprooted them on the day of Badr, and as for your paternal uncles, God granted them respite for a time. Mujahid, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said: They are the disbelievers of the Quraysh who were killed on the day of Badr. Malik narrated it in this way on the authority of Nafi` on the authority of Ibn `Umar. And His statement: And they have set up rivals for God to lead [people] astray from His way, meaning they have set up partners for Him whom they worship along with Him, and they have called people to that. Then the Most High said, threatening and warning them on the tongue of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, ‘Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire,’ meaning whatever you are able to do in this world, do it, for whatever it may be, for your destination is the Fire, meaning your return and abode is to Us, as the Most High said: We give them enjoyment for a little while, then We force them to a severe punishment, and the Most High said: Enjoyment in this world, then to Us is their return, then We will make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve.

14:31: The Almighty says, commanding His servants to obey Him, fulfill His right, and be kind to His creation by establishing prayer, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner, and to spend from what God has provided them by paying zakat, spending on relatives, and being kind to strangers. What is meant by establishing it is to maintain its time, its limits, its bowing, its humility, and its prostration. The Almighty commanded spending from what He has provided in secret, meaning in private, and in public, meaning in public, and to hasten to do so to save themselves before a day comes which is the Day of Resurrection in which there will be no selling or friendship meaning no ransom will be accepted from anyone by selling his soul, as the Almighty said: So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved and His saying: nor friendship Ibn Jarir said: He says that there is no friendship of a friend, so he forgives the one who deserves punishment for his disobedience, rather there is justice and equity, and friendship is a source from the saying of the one who says: I was a friend of so-and-so, so I am a friend of him, friendship and friendship, and from it is the saying Imru' al-Qais: I have turned away from them for fear of ruin, and I am not one to be stingy with my manners or my words. Qatada said: God knows that in this world there are sales and friendships that people make in this world, so a man should consider who he befriends and what he befriends. If it is for God, then let him continue, and if it is for someone other than God, then he will be cut off from him. I said: What is meant by this is that God the Almighty informs that no sale or ransom will benefit anyone, even if he were to ransom himself with the earth full of gold if he found it. No one’s friendship or intercession will benefit him if he meets God as a disbeliever. God the Almighty said: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be aided. And God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there will be no trading, nor friendship, nor intercession. And the disbelievers - it is they who are the wrongdoers.”
14:32: God Almighty enumerates His blessings upon His creation by creating for them the heavens as a protected roof and the earth as a bed. And He sent down water from the sky, and with it We produced pairs of diverse plants, including fruits and crops of different colors, shapes, tastes, smells, and benefits. And He subjected the ark by making it float on the current of the sea water, running on it by the command of God Almighty, and He subjected the sea to carry it so that travelers can travel with it from one region to another, bringing what is here to there, and what is there to here, and He subjected the rivers to split the earth from one country to another, providing sustenance for the servants of drink and water, and other types of benefits. And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, both diligently pursuing their courses. That is, they move without tiring, night or day. “It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day. Each, in an orbit, floats.” “He covers the night with the day, pursuing it rapidly. And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.” So the sun and the moon follow one another, and the night and the day conflict, so sometimes one takes from the other and becomes longer, then the other takes from the other and becomes shorter. “He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. That is God, your Lord.” And His statement, And He gave you of all that you asked Him for, means He prepared for you what you need in all your circumstances, from what you ask Him for in your circumstances. Some of the Salaf said: of all that you asked Him for and what you did not ask Him for. And some of them read, And He gave you of all that you asked Him for. And His statement, And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them, God the Almighty informs us of the inability of the servants to count the favors, let alone to thank Him for them, as Talq bin Habib, may God have mercy on him, said: Indeed, the right of God is heavier than the servants can bear, and indeed the favors of God are more than the servants can count, but they became repentant and spent the night repentant. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, O God, to You is praise that is not sufficient, nor is it deposited, nor is it dispensed with, our Lord. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Ismail bin Abi Al-Harith told us, Dawud bin Al-Muhber told us, Saleh Al-Mari told us, on the authority of Jaafar bin Zaid Al-Abdi, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “On the Day of Resurrection, three registers will be brought out for the son of Adam: a register in which are his good deeds, a register in which are his sins, and a register in which are the blessings from God Almighty upon him. God Almighty will say to the smallest of his blessings - I think he said in the register of blessings - ‘Take your price from his good deeds,’ so it will take up all of his good deeds, then it will step aside and say: ‘By Your glory, I have not taken it all,’ and the sins and blessings will remain. Then, when God wants to have mercy on him, He will say: ‘O My servant, I have multiplied your good deeds and overlooked your bad deeds’ - I think he said: ‘And I have bestowed My blessings upon you.’” It is strange and its chain of transmission is weak. It has been narrated in the hadith that David, peace be upon him, said: ‘O Lord, how can I thank You when my thanks to You is a blessing from You upon me?’ Then God Almighty said: Now you have thanked Me, O David, meaning when you have admitted your failure to thank the Benefactor. Imam Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Praise be to God, for whom gratitude for a blessing of His cannot be fulfilled except through a new blessing that requires its performer to thank Him for it. And the speaker said about that: If every part of me had a language to praise you for the good you have done If I had thanked you with it, my gratitude would have been more eloquent in kindness and favor.

14:35: In this context, God Almighty mentions, arguing with the polytheists of the Arabs, that the sacred city of Mecca was first established for the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, and that Abraham, because of whom it was inhabited, disavowed those who worshipped other than God, and that he prayed for security for Mecca, saying: My Lord, make this city secure, and God answered him, saying: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary? The verse, and God Almighty said: "Indeed, the first House established for mankind was that at Bakkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs, the station of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be secure." And He said in this story, My Lord, make this city secure, so He recognized it because he prayed with it after it was built, and for this reason He said: Praise be to God, who has given me, in my old age, Ishmael and Isaac. It is known that Ishmael was thirteen years older than Isaac, but when he went with Ishmael and his mother while he was an infant to the place of Mecca, he also prayed, saying: My Lord, make this city secure, as we mentioned there in Surat Al-Baqarah, in detail. And his saying: And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols Every supplicant should supplicate for himself, his parents and his offspring. Then he mentioned that many people were tempted by idols, and that he disavowed those who worshipped them and referred their matter to God. If He wills, He will punish them and if He wills, He will forgive them, like the saying of Jesus, peace be upon him: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. There is nothing more in it than referring it to the will of God Almighty, not permitting that to happen. Abdullah bin Wahb said: Amr bin Al-Harith told us that Bakr bin Sawadah told him on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Jarir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, recited the saying of Abraham, peace be upon him: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people the verse, and the saying of Jesus, peace be upon him: If You punish them, they are Your servants the verse, then he raised his hands and said: O God, my nation, O God, my nation, O God, my nation and he cried, so God said: Go, Gabriel, to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best, and ask him what makes you cry? Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told him what he had said. Then God said: Go to Muhammad and tell him: We will please you regarding your nation and will not displease you.

14:37: This indicates that this is a second supplication after the first supplication that he made when he left Hajar and her son, and that was before building the House, and this was after building it as confirmation and desire to God Almighty, and that is why he said: “At your sacred House.” And His saying: Our Lord, that they may establish prayer. Ibn Jarir said: It is connected to His saying: The sacred place. That is, You made it sacred so that its people could establish prayer there. So make hearts among the people incline toward them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair and others said: If He had said hearts among the people, the Persians, the Romans, the Jews, the Christians and all the people would have crowded around it, but He said: Of the people, so He singled out the Muslims for it. And His saying: And provide them with fruits, that is, so that this would be an aid to them in obeying You. And just as it is a valley without crops, then make fruits for it that they may eat. And God answered that as He said: Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary to which are brought the fruits of all things, a provision from Us? This is from His kindness, generosity, mercy and blessing that there is no fruitful tree in the sacred land of Mecca, and yet the fruits of what is around it are brought to it in response to the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him.
14:38: Ibn Jarir said: God Almighty says, informing about Abraham, His friend, that he said: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare, meaning You know my intention in my supplication, and what I intended by my supplication for the people of this country, but rather the intention is to please You and to be sincere to You, for You know all things, their outward and inward aspects, nothing of them is hidden from You on earth or in heaven. The verse, and He says: And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire and say, ‘Oh, would that we could be sent back and not deny the signs of our Lord.’ The verse, and God Almighty says: And they cry out therein. The verse, God Almighty says in response to their saying: Did you not swear before that there would be no cessation for you? That is, did you not swear before this state that there would be no cessation for you from what you are in and that there would be no resurrection or recompense? So taste this for that. Mujahid and others said: There would be no cessation for you. That is, you would not move from this world to the Hereafter, like His saying: And they swore. “By God, their most earnest oaths, God will not resurrect anyone who dies.” The verse, And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them and presented to you examples. That is, you have seen and heard what We inflicted on the nations who denied before you, and despite this, you did not take heed from them, and there was no deterrent for you in what We inflicted upon them. There is great wisdom, so what avail are warnings? Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abd al-Rahman that Ali, may God be pleased with him, said about this verse, And their plot was such that mountains would move. He said: The one who argued with Abraham about his Lord took two young eagles, and raised them until they grew strong and matured and became young men. He said: A man tied each one of them to a peg to a coffin and starved them, and he and another man sat in the coffin. He said: He raised a stick in the coffin over the meat on its head and they flew away, and he kept saying to his companion: Look what you see? He said: I see such and such until he said: I see the whole world as if it were a fly. He said: So he aimed the stick, and he aimed it, and they both fell down. He said: This is what God Almighty said: And their plot was such that mountains would move. Abu Ishaq said: And it is also in the recitation of Abdullah: And if their plot was… I said: And it was also narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them, that they read And if they almost as Ali read it, and it was also narrated by Sufyan al-Thawri and Isra’il from Abu Ishaq from Abd al-Rahman ibn Adhanan from Ali, so he mentioned something similar, and it was also narrated from Ikrimah that the context of this story is about Nimrod, the king of Canaan, that he sought the causes of the heavens with this trick and deceit, just as Pharaoh, the king of the Copts, sought to build a tower, but they failed and were weak, and they were less, more contemptible, smaller and more defeated. And Mujahid mentioned this story about Nebuchadnezzar, and that when his sight was cut off from the earth and its people, he was called: O tyrant, where are you going? So he was frightened, then he heard a voice above him, so he aimed the spears and the eagles aimed, so the mountains were terrified by their shaking, and the mountains almost moved from the sound of that, so that is his saying: And if their plot was such that the mountains would move from it. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujahid that he read it as that the mountains may pass away from it with the first lam open and the second damma. Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And if their plot was to remove the mountains from it he said: Their plot was not to remove the mountains from it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same, and Ibn Jarir explained it by saying that what they did to themselves of their associating partners with God and their disbelief in Him did not harm anything of the mountains or anything else, but rather the consequences of that returned upon them. I said: This is similar to the statement of God Almighty: “And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart, and you will never reach the mountains in height.” The second statement in its interpretation is what Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: And if their plot was to remove the mountains from it he said: Their associating partners with God is like His statement: The heavens almost burst from it the verse, and this is what Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said.
